transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-04 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~45 minutes
Attendees: Lena Park (Redwood AE), Samir Rao (Redwood SE), Maya Singh (Holosystems, Head of ML), Daniel Ortiz (Holosystems, CTO), Priya Patel (Holosystems, Dev Lead)

[00:00] Lena Park: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick agenda — we'll walk through the hosted API for chat and text generation basics, talk streaming, params, retries and then Q&A. Samir will demo the SDK and the console.
[00:20] Maya Singh: Hi Lena, hi Samir. Thanks, excited to see latency numbers. We're building a customer-facing chat, need sub-300ms p95 ideally.
[00:30] Samir Rao: Great — we'll show a streaming example first, that's usually the lowest-latency path for chat. Note: streaming here means SSE-like chunked responses over the SDK or HTTP.
[01:02] Daniel Ortiz: Quick one — is streaming supported in all regions? We have EU data residency concerns.
[01:18] Samir Rao: Yes, hosted supports region pinning; we can route to EU regions. For regulated data we usually suggest Private or Dedicated but hosted can be configured for certain customers. We'll follow up with the network diagram in the security packet.
[01:45] Priya Patel: And in terms of retries — if a chunk fails mid-stream, do you retry or re-request? That's important for idempotency.
[02:05] Samir Rao: Good question. For streaming we recommend client-side reconnect with an idempotency key and resume using the cached KV cache prefix where possible. In practice we provide sequence tokens so you can re-request from an offset. Small caveat — sometimes transcriptions call it KV cash or KV cache in docs, which is confusing.
[02:40] Maya Singh: ha, yes saw that in the doc export.
[03:00] Samir Rao: Demo time — I'll share my screen. (screen share) Here's a simple JS snippet using our SDK: createChatStream({model: "redwood-chat-lite-1", messages, stream: true, max_tokens: 512, temperature: 0.2}) — note the params.
[03:35] Samir Rao: So max_tokens caps generation, temperature controls randomness, top_p is nucleus sampling. For chat you often keep temperature low for deterministic replies.
[04:10] Lena Park: We also add retry guidance in the quickstart — exponential backoff + jitter, and use idempotency keys for non-streaming completions. For streaming specifically, we recommend stateless resume tokens.
[04:40] Daniel Ortiz: What's the default rate limit / quota for hosted? We might need predictable throughput during peak times.
[05:02] Lena Park: Default is tier-based. For pilot we'll increase quotas; Dedicated gives SLA-backed throughput. We can include sample throughput numbers in the pricing doc.
[05:30] Priya Patel: Can you show the console for per-route token cost and latency breakdown?
[05:50] Samir Rao: Sure — switching to the console -> routes -> demo-chat. Here you get token-level cost, p50/p95 latencies, and breakdown by model. There's also a traces tab for individual requests.
[06:30] Samir Rao: Another useful Optimize feature is batching suggestions — if you're doing many short prompts, the console suggests batch sizes to reduce unit cost while keeping latency targets.
[07:05] Maya Singh: About model variants and fallbacks — we want to fail from the high-capacity model to a smaller cheaper one if load spikes. Does hosted support automated fallback?
[07:25] Lena Park: Yes — smart routing policies let you define fallback chains (redwood-chat-high -> redwood-chat-lite). You can choose latency-first or cost-first policies. We also support regional fallback.
[08:00] Daniel Ortiz: Any tips on prompt caching? We have many repeated prefixes for personalization.
[08:20] Samir Rao: Prefix caching via KV cache (we sometimes see docs say KV cash) — keep static system prompts cached and only call the model for user turns. This reduces tokens and latency. For some workloads you can also use our server-side prefix cache configured per route.
[09:00] Priya Patel: How do you handle hallucinations / safety?
[09:15] Samir Rao: We provide content filters, safety labels, and eval tooling to monitor regressions. If you need deterministic outputs, you can lower temperature and add guardrails in the prompt or use function/tool calling to constrain outputs.
[10:00] Maya Singh: Can the SDK stream partial structured JSON? We want to incrementally render chunks.
[10:18] Samir Rao: Yes, streaming supports structured outputs. We have examples with chunked JSON and a 'final' flag to indicate completion. Be cautious with partial parsing — we put a strong versioning note in the docs.
[11:00] (brief cross-talk)
[11:25] Daniel Ortiz: For retries on non-idempotent generation, is there a recommended pattern? We do few-shot summarization that could duplicate outputs on retries.
[11:45] Samir Rao: Use idempotency keys for request-level retries. For operations that change state you should implement server-side dedupe or client-side confirm semantics. We'll include a snippet.
[12:20] Lena Park: Sending link to the deck now, and the quickstart repo: https://redwood.example/deck and https://github.com/redwood-inference/quickstarts — (note: links may appear truncated in transcript).
[12:50] Maya Singh: Thank you. A few compliance questions — do you support customer-managed keys (KMS/HSM)?
[13:05] Lena Park: Yes — for Private we integrate with customer KMS/HSM. For hosted we support envelope encryption + customer KMS for certain enterprise tiers. We'll share the SOC2/ISO docs.
[13:40] Priya Patel: What's retention policy for prompts and responses? We need RU-3 compliance for data retention ranges.
[13:55] Samir Rao: Hosted retains logs for a default period, configurable on enterprise tiers. For the POC we can set retention to your policy and provide an export.
[14:30] Maya Singh: Great. One more — how do you measure token billing vs embeddings? We're mostly token generation.
[14:50] Lena Park: Tokens for generation, embeddings billed differently. Console shows token counts per call; Optimize suggests quantization and batching to reduce unit cost.
[15:20] Samir Rao: Back to the demo — here's a live stream of a user query. Notice chunk sizes and how the client renders partial responses. (streaming)
[16:00] Stream chunk: "Hello, thanks for reaching out..."
[16:30] Priya Patel: We're seeing ~180ms p50 in this demo, good. How much overhead does SDK add?
[16:45] Samir Rao: Minimal — SDK is thin. Most latency is network + model compute. We recommend colocating in same region and using persistent connections for best p95.
[17:10] Maya Singh: On the POC, we'd like to run a 1k-conversation benchmark with real traffic patterns. Can you help?
[17:30] Lena Park: Absolutely — Samir will provide benchmark scripts. We'll also include guidance for warm KV cache, batching settings, and quantization recommendations.
[18:05] Daniel Ortiz: Any hard limits on max_tokens? Some of our long-form generation needs 2k-4k tokens.
[18:25] Samir Rao: Our models support up to 8k in many variants; some high-capacity models go higher. We'll check model-specific limits and call them out in the model catalog.
[19:00] Priya Patel: Regarding SDKs — do you have Python/JS examples for retries and streaming?
[19:15] Samir Rao: Yes — quickstart repo includes both. We also have a retry helper in the SDK that handles exponential backoff and idempotency for non-streaming calls.
[19:50] Maya Singh: What about observability during POC? We need traces and per-user request linking.
[20:10] Lena Park: Console supports trace IDs and you can pass request metadata that shows up in our traces. We also have an API to pull logs.
[20:40] (short pause)
[21:00] Samir Rao: Quick note on rate limiting: for hosted we have soft limits and can grant spikes; Dedicated gets predictable capacity. For short spikes consider burst capacity or autoscale in Dedicated.
[21:35] Daniel Ortiz: Is Dedicated required for our SLA or can hosted suffice?
[21:50] Lena Park: It depends on your required SLOs. Hosted is great for speed to value, but Dedicated provides guaranteed throughput and isolation. For many teams we start with hosted pilot then move to Dedicated if they need the guaranteed numbers.
[22:30] Priya Patel: Can we test fallback behavior during our POC? We want to simulate a high-load event and see automated fallback.
[22:45] Samir Rao: Yes — we'll help script a load test that triggers fallback and collect the logs.
[23:10] Maya Singh: About security docs — can you share the network diagram and list of endpoints?
[23:25] Lena Park: We'll attach the network diagram in the security packet. Also note our API endpoints are region-specific and we'll provide prefix lists for firewall allow-lists.
[24:00] (noise / slight overlap, transcription imperfect)
[24:30] Daniel Ortiz: Any partner integrations for monitoring? We use Datadog.
[24:45] Samir Rao: We have Datadog hooks and can export metrics via Prometheus-compatible endpoints.
[25:10] Priya Patel: Does the hosted API sanitize logs or PII automatically?
[25:25] Samir Rao: We don't automatically redact PII — we recommend application-level redaction before sending if PII is sensitive. For some enterprise tiers we can help with redaction pipelines.
[26:00] (crosstalk)
[26:30] Maya Singh: Ok, thinking about success criteria — low-latency p95, < $0.01 per convo for core flows, and no retention beyond 30 days for POC. We'll put that in an email.
[27:00] Lena Park: Perfect. We'll confirm those in the POC charter.
[27:20] Samir Rao: Demo: showing how to configure retries: snippet uses maxRetries: 3, backoff: "exponential", jitter: true. For completions set idempotencyKey for safe retries.
[28:00] Priya Patel: If a streaming session disconnects, will the model re-generate overlapping tokens on resume?
[28:20] Samir Rao: The resume protocol uses sequence offsets to avoid overlap; however in practice clients should dedupe on client side — we've seen docs misread this as seamless resume but it's best-effort.
[28:50] Maya Singh: We might prefer whole-response retries instead of streaming resume, simpler to implement.
[29:05] Samir Rao: That works — the tradeoff is extra cost and latency on retries, but easier semantics.
[29:30] Daniel Ortiz: Can we get sample SLO docs?
[29:45] Lena Park: Yes — we'll include sample SLO and error budgets for pilot.
[30:10] (brief pause)
[30:30] Priya Patel: For cost optimization, you mentioned quantization and model recommendation — can Optimize suggest model/quant profiles automatically?
[30:45] Samir Rao: Optimize analyzes your workload and recommends quantization and model variants, plus batching/cache settings. It can simulate unit cost impact.
[31:20] Maya Singh: How do we measure quality regressions?
[31:35] Samir Rao: We tie evals to prompt sets; Optimize supports regression alerts when outputs deviate from baselines. You can upload test prompts and expected outputs.
[32:00] Lena Park: Ok wrapping up demo details — we'll attach the quickstart, sample benchmark script, and the security packet.
[32:20] Maya Singh: Any limitations we should know for long-term?
[32:35] Samir Rao: Model swaps require testing; also if you need on-prem for compliance, Private is the option. For now hosted should be fine for the POC.
[33:10] Daniel Ortiz: Rough timeline and costs for Dedicated?
[33:25] Lena Park: We'll send reserved capacity pricing in the pricing doc; Dedicated onboarding is typically 4–8 weeks depending on sizing.
[33:50] Priya Patel: Can you also send sample contract or terms?
[34:05] Lena Park: We'll include procurement checklist and sample terms in the follow-up.
[34:30] (ambient noise)
[34:55] Maya Singh: One last technical — is there any client-side buffering for streaming that causes latency spikes?
[35:10] Samir Rao: Buffering depends on chunk sizes; we recommend smaller chunk sizes for interactive UX. We'll include recommended chunk sizes in the benchmark script.
[35:40] Lena Park: Ok let's do a quick recap and next steps.
[36:00] Lena Park: Recap — demoed streaming SDK and console, discussed params (max_tokens, temperature, top_p), retries and idempotency, prefixes/KV cache, Optimize suggestions, and POC plan.
[36:25] Maya Singh: Sounds good. We'll prepare success criteria and the data subset.
[36:40] Daniel Ortiz: We'll share infra contacts for the kickoff.
[36:55] Priya Patel: Appreciate the benchmark scripts.
[37:10] Lena Park: Action items: I'll send pricing, Samir will drop the benchmark. We'll also send SOC2 and network diagram.
[37:30] (short confirmation noises)
[38:00] Samir Rao: I'll email the sample script and include instructions to warm the KV cache and run with/without batching to compare.
[38:25] Maya Singh: Great — expected timeframe for us to confirm POC? 1 week to align?
[38:40] Lena Park: That works; we'll tentatively kick off next Wednesday 2026-03-11.
[39:00] Daniel Ortiz: Thanks everyone.
[39:15] (meeting winds down)
[39:40] Transcript notes: automatic transcription — some words may be misrecognized (e.g., KMSs, KV cash). Links and exact code may be truncated.
[40:00] End of call.
